project.name: ORISO-Database
project.description: Central ORISO database architecture and operations repository containing service-owned MariaDB schema exports, MongoDB dumps, Matrix PostgreSQL docs, Redis/RabbitMQ docs, backup artifacts, and initialization jobs.

nodes.name: Timestamped backup layout
nodes.summary: Backups are organized by timestamp with paired MariaDB SQL gz and MongoDB archive gz files.

nodes.name: Redis cache and sessions
nodes.summary: Redis is used for Spring sessions, cache prefixes, tokens, and temporary/rate-limit data.

nodes.name: Consulting type MongoDB
nodes.summary: MongoDB stores consulting type and application settings documents; JSON/schema validation is documented as disabled.

nodes.name: Cross-service ids without FK enforcement
nodes.summary: Many agency_id, user_id, session_id, consulting_type, and tenant_id references cross service/database boundaries and are not enforced by MariaDB constraints.

nodes.name: Database initialize job
nodes.summary: database-initialize.yaml restores MariaDB and MongoDB from backup files copied into the job pod.

nodes.name: Liquibase disabled in services
nodes.summary: ORISO backend services do not auto-migrate schemas; this repository is the operational source of schema truth.

nodes.name: Manual schema exports
nodes.summary: Schema changes are applied manually to running databases, then exported back into mariadb/*/schema.sql.

nodes.name: Matrix-owned PostgreSQL
nodes.summary: PostgreSQL is dedicated to Matrix Synapse and is not part of ORISO service schema ownership.

nodes.name: phpMyAdmin read-only access
nodes.summary: k8s/mariadb-client exposes phpMyAdmin through ingress, basic auth, and a view-only database user.

nodes.name: RabbitMQ auto-created topology
nodes.summary: Services create queues/exchanges/bindings at runtime; repository documents operations but not definitions.

nodes.name: Environment drift
nodes.summary: Docs mix ClusterIPs, localhost with hostNetwork, and service DNS names; generated cluster metadata appears in operational docs/manifests.

nodes.name: Missing tenant/id indexes
nodes.summary: Several tenant_id and *_id columns used for filtering or cross-service joins are not indexed in exported schemas.

nodes.name: MongoDB auth and validation gap
nodes.summary: MongoDB docs state no authentication and disabled JSON schema validation for consulting types.

nodes.name: No executable migration history
nodes.summary: The repo stores schema snapshots and DATABASECHANGELOG tables, but not the actual ordered migration files for each service.

nodes.name: Sensitive dumps in repository
nodes.summary: The targeted SQL dump contains user, consultant, session, notification, Matrix id, email, and password-like values.

nodes.name: Static secrets and default credentials
nodes.summary: Docs and YAML include root/default credentials and system user password material; these should be externalized or rotated.

nodes.name: Service-owned databases
nodes.summary: Each backend service owns its MariaDB database and service user, limiting schema ownership by service boundary.

nodes.name: System user seed job
nodes.summary: system-users-job.yaml creates Matrix users and userservice.user rows for platform system accounts.

nodes.name: tenant_id convention
nodes.summary: Tenant ownership is represented by tenant_id columns across schemas, without cross-database foreign keys to tenantservice.tenant.

nodes.name: UserService relational core
nodes.summary: userservice stores users, consultants, sessions, chats, assignments, notifications, audits, and Matrix/Rocket.Chat linkage.

tour.title: Start with the platform boundary
tour.description: README.md explains the repository responsibility: backend services have Liquibase disabled, so this repo is the manual source of truth for database schemas and operations.

tour.title: Understand MariaDB ownership
tour.description: Each service has a MariaDB database export. userservice is the largest schema; tenantservice owns the tenant registry; cross-service relationships are mostly id conventions rather than database-enforced foreign keys.

tour.title: Trace users and sessions
tour.description: userservice.user, userservice.consultant, and userservice.session are the counseling core. Session metadata fans out into topics, supervisors, chats, uploads, notifications, and video rooms.

tour.title: Trace tenant isolation
tour.description: tenant_id appears in tenant-aware tables, but there is no cross-database foreign key to tenantservice.tenant. Backend services must enforce tenant boundaries consistently.

tour.title: Review non-relational stores
tour.description: MongoDB stores consulting type/application settings documents, Matrix owns PostgreSQL, Redis stores cache/session data, and RabbitMQ owns messaging topology at runtime.

tour.title: Review initialization and backup
tour.description: Timestamped backups pair MariaDB SQL gz and MongoDB archive gz files. database-initialize.yaml restores from archives copied into the job pod; system-users-job.yaml seeds Matrix and userservice system users.

tour.title: Review the risk map
tour.description: The biggest risks are sensitive dumps in git, static/default secrets, missing indexes on tenant/id columns, no executable migration history, and environment drift between ClusterIP, localhost, and service DNS usage.
